title: Signing the Europe contract and the voyage over
summary: The contract was signed at four in the morning in early 1925 and the band, with wives and friends, had a carefree crossing in summer.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So, anyway, Lenidow came in at ten o'clock, right?
Well, we signed the contract that night about four o'clock in the morning.
This is late 1924, or when was this?
This is late 19 -- well, no, it was the beginning of 1925.
Yeah. See, because we went over in that July, or that August, see. And opened up in Berlin in either August or September.
Uh hunh. So, how did the trip go?
The trip? Oh, we had fun going over the water. See that was the first -- well, I'd been in the war, you know.

But we had a -- the guys were slipping in and out of other peoples bunks, because we had fun there. Others were gambling all the time. So, we had a wonderful time. The band, see, didn't have to do no rehearsing because we knew what we was going to do . We'd been doing it for a year and a half, you know what I mean?

So we had our program all set. And all we had to do was -- and we couldn't -- the show wasn't together yet. See, they were rushing it. So there wasn't no music even for us to rehearse. So we just had a wonderful -- had a ball on the boat, you see. We all of us had a wonderful trip because we all had our wives and lady friends. And the only one that didn't make it was Teroy, the same trombone player I'm telling you about.
